model_policy.criterion: Lowest pooled recursive RMSE over the full 72-hour hold-out; MAE breaks ties.
model_policy.selected_models: XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, and Ridge are trained on identical features, splits, and backtest origins; the best learned model is persisted per city.
model_policy.baselines: Persistence and the diurnal statistical forecaster are reference baselines and runtime fallbacks, not production candidates.

not_evaluated.ARIMA/SARIMA: Univariate linear time-series models do not naturally use weather or other exogenous drivers, and multi-station data would require many separate fits.
not_evaluated.Prophet: Adds a large dependency and trend/seasonality assumptions that are hard to validate on 90 days of gap-prone hourly data; recursive 72-hour scoring is also awkward.
not_evaluated.LSTM/Transformer: Needs substantially more clean history and GPU/training budget than the free-tier deployment provides; harder to explain and slower to retrain daily.

selection.reason: Ridge regression had the lowest pooled recursive RMSE (42.32) and MAE (24.9) among learned candidates on identical chronological hold-out origins; persistence RMSE was 57.02 and the statistical baseline was 51.71.
